title: HK100 – 2027 course description and checkpoints
claims: The 2027 HK100 starts on Saturday 23 January 2027 at Pak Tam Chung and finishes after the descent of Tai Mo Shan, Hong Kong's highest peak at 957 m.
The course is 100 km, climbs over 5,000 m, and most of the climbing is in the second half.
The first 10 km follow the MacLehose Trail past High Island Reservoir to CP1 at East Dam (10 km).
For 2027 CP2 has been relocated to Sai Wan Pavilion at 17 km, before the beaches.
For 2027 CP3 has been relocated to Pak Tam Au at 28 km.
CP4 is at Pak Sha O (36 km) and CP5 at Yung Shue O (44 km).
CP6 is at Kei Ling Ha (52 km) and is the checkpoint with drop bags.
CP7 is at Gilwell Camp (65 km); the organiser calls CP6 to CP7 the race's longest and hardest stage.
CP8 is at Beacon Hill (74 km) and CP9 at Shing Mun (80 km).
CP10 is at Lead Mine Pass (87 km), is inaccessible to vehicles, and the text says runners then have 'just 10km to go'.
After the Tai Mo Shan summit there is a 4 km run downhill to the finish.
The page provides a direct download of the official course GPX file HK100-Full-2027.gpx.
The course is marked with directional arrows, crosses and reflective flagging tape, and runners are advised to download the GPX to a watch.
The course is rocky, uneven and steep in places, and the organiser warns runners to take care when overtaking and when crossing roads.
Emergency first aid will be available at each checkpoint.
Mobile phone coverage exists over most of the course but some areas have no coverage or only intermittent coverage.
The Food & Beverages section of the page says 'To be announced'.
